panels.title: Backend up
panels.description: Prometheus's own view of whether the backend's /metrics endpoint is scrapeable. 0 here means the scrape is failing - the process is down, wedged, or unreachable on the network.

panels.title: Process uptime
panels.description: How long the current backend process has been running. A value that keeps resetting to near-zero means the container is crash-looping.

panels.title: Request rate
panels.description: Requests per second across all routes, averaged over 5 minutes.

panels.title: Error rate (5xx)
panels.description: Share of requests returning a 5xx. This is the single most important number on this dashboard - it is the one that means users are actually seeing failures. 4xx is deliberately excluded: a 401/404 is usually a client doing something wrong, not the service being broken.

panels.title: Event-loop lag (p99)
panels.description: How long the Node event loop is blocked. Node is single-threaded: sustained lag here means requests are queueing behind synchronous work, and shows up as latency even when CPU looks fine.

panels.title: Request rate by route
panels.description: Per-route traffic. Route labels are Express route PATTERNS (/api/donations/:id), never concrete URLs - see backend/src/metrics.ts for why that matters.

panels.title: Latency p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Derived from the http_request_duration_seconds histogram. p95/p99 matter more than the average - an average hides the slow tail that users actually complain about.

panels.title: Responses by status code
panels.description: Splits traffic by HTTP status class, so a spike in 4xx (clients misbehaving / auth problems) is visually distinguishable from a spike in 5xx (the service itself failing).

panels.title: Node heap used
panels.description: Heap growth that never comes back down between GC cycles is the usual signature of a memory leak - which, under the container memory limits set in docker-compose.prod.yml / k8s manifests, ends in an OOM kill.

panels.title: Container CPU (cAdvisor)
panels.description: Container-level CPU from cAdvisor - the layer the application cannot report on itself. Useful for correlating an application latency spike with the container actually being CPU-throttled against its limit. NOTE: empty on Docker Desktop for Mac - cAdvisor cannot resolve container NAMES there (it needs containerd's socket, which Docker Desktop does not expose to the host), so it emits only cgroup ids. Works normally on a Linux host. See docs/MONITORING.md.

panels.title: Container memory (cAdvisor)
panels.description: Container-level memory from cAdvisor. Compare against the mem_limit values in docker-compose.prod.yml - approaching the limit is what precedes an OOM kill. NOTE: same Docker Desktop for Mac caveat as the CPU panel - see docs/MONITORING.md.
